picks.what: Woodcut in Hartmann Schedel’s Nuremberg Chronicle
picks.why: labeled GENUA; true view of the harbor with the Lanterna lighthouse and the mole

picks.what: Engraving in Braun and Hogenberg, Civitates Orbis Terrarum, vol. 1
picks.why: colored panorama of the city and harbor from the sea, already cropped to Genoa; this copy from the 1582 edition

picks.file: Bastian Stoopendal, Pieter Mortier, Alessandro Baratta, Veduta di Genova, fine XVII secolo.jpg
picks.what: Bird’s-eye view from the sea, engraving in Mortier’s Nouveau Théâtre de l’Italie
picks.why: large panorama of the whole city, harbor and moles; published 1704

picks.what: The city seen from the Darsena harbor, etching
picks.why: only P3 view showing the city along the harbor rather than a single building

picks.file: Flickr - …trialsanderrors - Piazza Acquaverde, Genoa, Italy, ca. 1895.jpg
picks.what: Piazza Acquaverde and the Columbus monument, photochrom print (Library of Congress)
picks.why: color; Columbus monument with the city climbing the hill behind

picks.file: Gênes - vue panoramique du côté du levant - btv1b90546371.jpg
picks.what: Rooftops of the old city looking east, press photograph (Agence Meurisse)
picks.why: general view over the old town with the Carignano dome; dated April 1922

picks.file: View of Genoa from the archiepiscopal seminary 003.JPG
picks.what: The city and harbor from above, photograph

notes: #28’s Commons license is the Flickr uploader’s CC BY 2.0; the photochrom itself is public domain (LoC), so PD may be used if preferred. #30 (Armanino color panorama of the harbor with the Lanterna) is the best P4 general view but Rijksmuseum dates it only ‘ca. 1880–1920’. #40 (Brogi panorama) is dated only ‘before 1925’. #4–#6 are 1929 photos misread as 1389, and show the Bisagno valley. #25 (Villa del Principe, ‘ante 1769’) skipped: single building and vague date.
